items.title: Profile
items.text: CX AI Lead at Volvo Cars and applied-AI product leader with roughly 25 years across enterprise software, product management, AI entrepreneurship, consulting, Customer Experience, and transformation. Former Co-founder, CEO, and Head of Product of a Chalmers Ventures-backed predictive-AI startup. Strongest as a builder-leader who combines enterprise-scale direction with hands-on agent, prompt, context, tool, evaluation, and workflow engineering.

items.title: Volvo Cars — CX AI Lead
items.text:
**April 2026–present · Gothenburg, Sweden**

- Leads AI strategy across Volvo Cars Customer Experience, from opportunity discovery and roadmaps to responsible-AI governance and build-versus-buy decisions.
- Owns CX Intelligence, the principal initiative, end to end, spanning product vision, data and solution architecture, proof-of-concept development, stakeholder alignment, legal considerations, and market enablement.
- Builds a shared customer-data foundation and AI-enriched topic taxonomy so markets, Commercial, Quality, and R&D can understand customer pain points through a common language and connect insight to action.
- The working proof of concept classifies Customer Care interactions into a governed topic catalog and scores customer friction; Microsoft Foundry agents analyze sentiment, self-service coverage, and related social conversations, then synthesize findings and recommend actions. It is moving into beta, not production.
- Co-initiated and facilitates a cross-functional AI learning community that helps commercial teams share work, document learning, identify overlaps, and avoid building in silos.

items.title: Volvo Cars — Digital, Customer Care, CRM, and AI leadership
items.text:
**November 2017–March 2026 · Sweden and United States**

#### Americas CRM transformation

- Led the cross-functional bridge between Volvo Cars' U.S. and Swedish digital and process organizations for the move from a long-standing bespoke Oracle CRM to Salesforce.
- Mapped current and future processes, represented global process owners in day-to-day decisions, transferred knowledge of Volvo's Salesforce customizations, shaped training content, and supported go-live and hypercare.
- Delivered an on-schedule launch without major operational disruption, onboarding approximately 40–50 agents in an operation handling roughly 300,000–500,000 cases annually; smaller launch issues were resolved during the first two weeks.

#### Global Customer Care platforms and processes

- As part of Volvo Cars' central global process team, helped improve Customer Care processes, procedures, and Salesforce Service Cloud capabilities used by more than 500 agents across over 20 markets, with some hands-on experience of Five9 contact-center telephony in support operations.
- Partnered with regional hubs responsible for local QA, training, and onboarding while driving global consistency across an ecosystem handling approximately three million customer interactions annually.
- Contributed to the broader Customer Care transformation during a period when global five-out-of-five top-box CSAT improved from approximately 78% to 85%; this was a shared organizational outcome.
- Helped build a retailer case-management portal connecting central Customer Care and National Sales Companies with hundreds of retailers across roughly ten European markets.

#### Care by Volvo — Head of Fleet Services

- Initially managed more than ten process owners defining the subscription-vehicle lifecycle across ordering, delivery, service, roadside assistance, damage repair, and return.
- Continued supporting Care by Volvo across successive roles, contributing to every EMEA market launch—approximately 15 markets—through process development and enablement for National Sales Companies and retailers.
- Led a secure Salesforce-based retailer collaboration capability that began with Care by Volvo and expanded into a standard tool for broader Customer Care and National Sales Company operations.

#### Organizer — Business Owner

- Packaged Volvo's in-house workshop-planning system for broader use across the global retail network, coordinating service demand with technicians, specialist tools, lifts, and workshop capacity.

items.title: CX Intelligence — governed AI topic classification
items.text:
**Status:** Working proof of concept moving into beta; not production.

Turns governed Customer Care and survey signals into evidence-backed intelligence about customer friction: where customers hit effort, confusion, repeat contact, or failed self-service. Each customer topic carries its evidence, a Customer Friction Score, sentiment, weekly trends, market and vehicle-model heat maps, related social conversations, and self-service coverage, plus a recommended next step that can be "keep watching." A daily Pulse edition summarizes what is worth following.

Topics are not embedding clusters. A language model proposes topics with defining conditions and include/exclude guidance into a versioned catalog, and a shortlist-and-verify classifier links each contact to every topic whose condition it shows. A model identifies friction outcomes; deterministic code computes scores, counts, and coverage.

The design principle is that agents think and the backend decides. Microsoft Foundry worker agents propose, independent reviewer agents challenge, and deterministic policy over governed Snowflake procedures activates changes with versioning and one-step rollback. The target operating model replaces routine approval queues with people who comment, flag, pause, and roll back. Models are chosen per task and compared on the same frozen inputs for correctness, evidence support, unsupported claims, latency, failure rate, and cost.

Production adoption and business impact have not yet been measured.

items.title: j-skills — skills for coding agents
items.text:
**Status:** Active, public, MIT-licensed, and used daily.

Ten skills for Claude Code, Codex CLI, and GitHub Copilot CLI. The core `workflow` skill takes a coding task through brainstorm, plan, execute, review, and wrap, with saved run state so a fresh session can resume, a reviewer normally from a different model vendor, and per-step model routing. Supporting skills cover app verification, durable memory, session retrospectives, cited HTML explainers, plain-language rewriting, and writing instructions for agents.

The `evals` skill grades candidate reviewer models against golden sets for bug detection and false alarms, so model-routing changes are measured before adoption rather than silently self-modifying. It evolved from John's earlier private workflow methodology.

**Scale on 15 October 2026:** ten skills, 79 tracked files, and 71 commits since 3 October 2026; plugin version 2.2.0.

**Public repository:** [github.com/johnviklund/j-skills](https://github.com/johnviklund/j-skills)

items.title: Agent CV — this site
items.text:
**Status:** Public, MIT-licensed, deployed, and actively maintained.

The résumé itself is an AI system: reviewed Markdown evidence is bundled into a Cloudflare Worker prompt, visitor transcripts stay untrusted, and upstream OpenAI events are normalized into a small public SSE contract. Human pages, raw Markdown, agent discovery files, structured metadata, expiring role links, bounded public-repository snapshots, and a private 90-day conversation archive all share the same grounded source boundary. The medium demonstrates the claim that John builds applied AI systems while remaining useful when the model API is unavailable.

**Public repository:** [github.com/johnviklund/agent-cv](https://github.com/johnviklund/agent-cv)

items.title: oma-space-launch — a desktop widget built with coding agents
items.text:
**Status:** Public, MIT-licensed, actively maintained, and listed as a verified community plugin in the official Omarchy plugin directory since 16 October 2026.

An Omarchy bar-widget plugin that shows a persistent countdown to the next SpaceX launch in the desktop top bar, with a click-to-open detail panel for the next launch and the following three. It reads the public Launch Library 2 API, caches results for at most 15 minutes, and shows a visible stale state instead of silently presenting old data as current.

Built in QML, JavaScript, and shell, with offline fixtures for exact, window-only, and unscheduled launch times. Development follows John's j-skills workflow: brainstorm, plan, execute, review, and wrap, one run per roadmap initiative.

**Scale on 16 October 2026:** version 1.2.0, 51 tracked files, and 80 commits since 13 September 2026.

**Omarchy plugin directory:** [Space Launch](https://plugins.omarchy.org/plugin.html?id=oma-space-launch), installable with `omarchy plugin add https://github.com/johnviklund/oma-space-launch.git --enable`

**Public repository:** [github.com/johnviklund/oma-space-launch](https://github.com/johnviklund/oma-space-launch)
